about: Built-in embodiment cards (llm_card.py). A client may send one of these names as "embodiment", or nothing when its request has the card's keys. The frames and image directions of libero_franka were measured in vla-eval's LIBERO images (rotated 180 degrees from robosuite's render, as openpi's LIBERO example does) and hold for the tabletop scenes: libero_spatial, libero_goal and libero_10's kitchen scenes; libero_object (a floor scene) and libero_10's study and living-room scenes put the table elsewhere.

cards.name: libero_franka
cards.docs:
One Franka Panda arm with a parallel-jaw gripper in a LIBERO tabletop scene, 20 control steps per second. World frame in metres: +z is up; the robot base stands at about x = -0.66, y = 0 and reaches forward along +x. The table top is at about z = 0.90 and the lowest grasp point is z = 0.91; small objects on the table are grasped at about z = 0.91 to 0.94. The grasp point (between the two finger pads) reaches at most 0.75 m horizontally from the base axis.
move_to takes the grasp point's x, y, z, the hand's orientation as rot6d (the first two columns of its rotation matrix in the world frame: r00, r10, r20, then r01, r11, r21) and the gripper, 0 open and 1 closed. The hand starts pointing straight down with the jaws opening along world y. Leave r00 to r21 unnamed to keep the orientation. To turn the hand about the vertical by an angle t, rotate both columns about z: each column (cx, cy, cz) becomes (cx cos t - cy sin t, cx sin t + cy cos t, cz); a quarter turn makes the jaws open along world x.
eef_state is x, y, z, the six rot6d values and the gripper command. gripper_qpos holds the two finger positions (about +0.04 and -0.04 when fully open): fingers that stopped apart after closing mean that something is between them.
After each motion the arm keeps tracking its last target until it arrives within 4 mm and 2 degrees or stops making progress, and a gripper change gets 15 more steps, before you see the next observation. A target the arm cannot reach shows as a remaining offset.
Images: agentview is a third-person camera facing the robot across the table, the robot at the top of the image; world +x points toward the bottom of the image and world +y toward the LEFT. wrist is a camera on the hand looking down; at the start orientation world +x points toward the top of this image and +y toward the right, and the image turns with the hand. The fingertips show as dark shapes at its bottom edge; a point on the table directly under the grasp point shows horizontally centred, about 60% of the way down. Near the table 1 cm is about 5 pixels of the 224-pixel wrist image: hover 10 to 15 cm above an object and use this view to correct x and y. Estimate every position from the images: there is no depth and no object-position query.
Grasping: the jaws open about 8 cm. A bowl is too wide to span: grasp it by its rim, one pad inside and one outside the wall, low enough that the pads overlap the wall, with the jaws closing across the wall. Travel at z = 1.10 or higher when you carry an object or pass over objects, and go down vertically. A held object hangs below the grasp point: release it a few centimetres above the surface it goes onto. The episode ends by itself when the task is done or its time runs out; you cannot declare success.
